Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Settings/FuelioI.overview: Settings UI for migrating a Fuelio CSV export into FuelTrack. It presents currency and active-vehicle options, opens a document picker for CSV/plain text, then calls FuelioCSVImporter and inserts Vehicle, FillUp, CarCost, and SavedStation rows into SwiftData. This is the user-facing half of tour step 10 (Fuelio Import and Export).

sections.title: Environment and import state
sections.explanation: The view pulls `modelContext`, `dismiss`, and `ActiveVehicleStore` from the environment, and reads the app-wide default currency from `@AppStorage`. Local `@State` tracks the file picker, chosen currency, whether to activate the imported vehicle, progress, and success/error copy. Keeping import UI state local keeps the form self-contained while still sharing the global model and active-vehicle services.

sections.title: Form and file picker
sections.explanation: The form explains how to export from Fuelio, lets the user pick a currency and an “set as active” toggle, then triggers `fileImporter` for `.commaSeparatedText`, `.plainText`, or `.data`. On appear, currency is seeded from the stored default. Success and failure paths clear the opposite message so the Result and Error sections stay mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Parse and insert records
sections.explanation: `importFile` security-scopes the picked URL, parses with `FuelioCSVImporter.parse`, then inserts a new `Vehicle` plus fill-ups, car costs, and favourite stations—all stamped with the chosen currency. After `modelContext.save()`, it optionally selects the vehicle via `activeVehicleStore` and builds a pluralized status string that also reports skipped invalid rows. Errors surface as localized descriptions without leaving partial UI state hanging (`isImporting` is cleared in `defer`).

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelTrackBack.overview: Defines the versioned FuelTrackBackup JSON schema and turns live SwiftData graphs into a portable snapshot. Format version 2 includes nested trips and trip points alongside vehicles, personal spend, budgets, and custom categories. Tour step 11 (Native Backup Round-Trip) starts here on the encode side.

sections.title: Format and root snapshot
sections.explanation: `formatName` and `formatVersion` are the contract the importer validates. `Snapshot` is a Codable envelope: format string, version, export timestamp, then arrays for vehicles and personal-finance records. Marking the structs `Sendable` keeps the DTO layer usable across concurrency boundaries without tying them to SwiftData models.

sections.title: VehicleBackup and decoder
sections.explanation: `VehicleBackup` mirrors vehicle identity, DVLA/compliance fields, and nested collections. The custom `init(from:)` is the compatibility hinge: `trips` uses `decodeIfPresent` and defaults to `[]`, so older v1 backups that omit trips still decode. Explicit `CodingKeys` keep encode/decode stable as fields grow.

sections.title: Nested backup DTOs
sections.explanation: Trip, trip-point, fill-up, car-cost, reminder, station, personal-expense, budget, and custom-category structs are plain Codable value types. Enums and SwiftData relationships are flattened to strings, UUIDs, and optional coordinates so the file is self-describing and independent of the live model graph.

sections.title: Snapshot build and file write
sections.explanation: `makeSnapshot` sorts each collection for deterministic output, then `exportJSON` encodes with pretty printing, sorted keys, and ISO-8601 dates. `writeBackupFile` drops an atomically written temp file named with a local timestamp stamp—handy for the share sheet without inventing a permanent on-disk archive location.

sections.title: Model-to-DTO mappers
sections.explanation: Private helpers map each SwiftData type onto its backup DTO, converting enums via `rawValue` and using sorted relationship accessors (`sortedFillUps`, `sortedCosts`, `sortedPoints`). Category keys and trip status stay as strings so restore can rehydrate enums with fallbacks. This keeps export logic centralized and free of view concerns.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelTrackBack.overview: Parses FuelTrackBackup JSON, validates format/version, and idempotently upserts every record into SwiftData by UUID. It is the restore counterpart to the exporter and powers the Settings backup import flow in tour step 11.

sections.title: Errors and result summary
sections.explanation: `FuelTrackBackupImportError` covers unreadable JSON, wrong format name, and unsupported versions with user-facing copy. `FuelTrackBackupImportResult` tallies inserts/updates across entity kinds and builds a pluralized `summary` string used by the Settings UI after a successful restore.

sections.title: Parse and orchestrate import
sections.explanation: `parse` decodes with ISO-8601 dates, then requires `format == FuelTrackBackup` and a version between 1 and the current exporter version. `importSnapshot` upserts custom categories first, then each vehicle and its children, then personal expenses and budgets, and finally saves once. `importData` is a thin parse-then-import convenience.

sections.title: Upsert vehicle and children
sections.explanation: Each upsert fetches by UUID predicate: existing rows are updated in place; missing rows are inserted with the backup’s id. Vehicle fields (including compliance) are always overwritten from the snapshot. Fill-ups, car costs, reminders, and saved stations follow the same insert-or-update pattern and re-attach the parent vehicle—making re-import safe.

sections.title: Personal finance upserts
sections.explanation: Personal expenses and budgets are top-level (not nested under a vehicle). Expense category is restored via `categoryKey` / enum fallbacks; budgets treat an empty category string as an overall monthly limit. Currency decoding defaults to GBP when raw values are unknown.

sections.title: Trips and custom categories
sections.explanation: Updating a trip deletes existing points before re-inserting the backup’s GPS samples, avoiding duplicate sequences on re-import. New trips are created with status decoded from the stored raw string. Custom categories restore name, SF Symbol, and car/personal scope so SpendCategoryCatalog can resolve them after restore.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Settings/BackupI.overview: Settings screen that restores a FuelTrack backup JSON via the document picker. It wires `FuelTrackBackupImporter` into SwiftData and can activate the first restored vehicle—completing the native backup round-trip UI in tour step 11.

sections.title: State and form UI
sections.explanation: Like the Fuelio import screen, this form explains the idempotent-by-ID restore behavior, offers a toggle to activate the first restored vehicle, and uses `fileImporter` limited to JSON/data types. Progress, result, and error sections mirror the Fuelio flow so Settings import experiences stay consistent.

sections.title: Security-scoped restore
sections.explanation: `importFile` accesses the security-scoped URL, parses then imports the snapshot, and optionally selects the first vehicle UUID from the snapshot via a SwiftData fetch. Status text comes from `result.summary`; any thrown importer or I/O error becomes `errorMessage`. `defer` always clears `isImporting` and stops security-scoped access when started.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/CarCost.swift.overview: SwiftData model for vehicle-linked non-fuel expenses (service, MOT, insurance, and custom categories). It is a core Spend-tab entity in tour step 12 and also appears in Fuelio CSV import and native backups.

sections.title: Stored properties and relationship
sections.explanation: `@Model` persists id, title, date, optional odometer, amount, raw currency/category strings, note, and createdAt, plus an optional `vehicle` relationship. Storing currency and category as raw strings keeps SwiftData schema simple while typed accessors sit above the persistence layer.

sections.title: Init and typed accessors
sections.explanation: The initializer accepts either a built-in `CostCategory` or an explicit `categoryKey` (used for custom catalog keys). `currencyCode` and `category` bridge to enums with `.gbp` / `.other` fallbacks; `categoryKey` exposes the raw string for catalog resolution and backup round-trips without losing custom ids.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/PersonalExpense.overview: SwiftData models for personal (non-vehicle) spending and monthly budgets. Together with car costs they extend FuelTrack into personal finance for tour step 12 (Spend and Personal Budgets).

sections.title: PersonalExpense model
sections.explanation: `PersonalExpense` stores title, date, amount, currency, category, note, payment method, and createdAt—no vehicle link. Typed `currencyCode` and `category` accessors wrap raw strings; `categoryKey` lets the spend catalog resolve built-in or custom keys the same way car costs do.

sections.title: PersonalBudget model
sections.explanation: `PersonalBudget` holds a monthly limit and currency. An empty `categoryRaw` means an overall budget (`isOverall`); a non-empty value scopes the limit to a `PersonalExpenseCategory`. That empty-string convention is what backup import restores when `category` is blank in JSON.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/SpendCategory.overview: Resolves built-in and custom spend categories into display metadata for car and personal scopes. Views and summaries use this catalog instead of hard-coding category enums—central to tour step 12.

sections.title: Resolved category type
sections.explanation: `ResolvedSpendCategory` is a lightweight, identifiable DTO with storage id, display name, SF Symbol, and whether it is custom. Separating resolution from SwiftData models lets lists and pickers share one presentation type.

sections.title: Catalog resolve helpers
sections.explanation: Custom keys are namespaced with a `c:` UUID prefix so they never collide with built-in raw values. `builtins` maps `CostCategory` or `PersonalExpenseCategory` by scope; `all` appends sorted custom categories for that scope. `resolve` looks up a key in the combined list and falls back to a synthetic “Other”/raw-key row so orphaned keys still render.

sections.title: Category spend row
sections.explanation: `CategorySpendRow` packages a resolved category with period total, all-time total, and entry count for summary UIs. Keeping aggregation fields on a separate struct leaves the catalog focused on identity and display while lists can still show rollups.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Costs/SpendRootV.overview: Root of the Spend tab: a segmented Car/Personal switcher that hosts car-cost and personal-expense lists, plus sheets for add forms, budgets, and custom categories. This is the navigation hub for tour step 12.

sections.title: SpendScope enum
sections.explanation: `SpendScope` is a simple `CaseIterable` picker model with Car and Personal titles. Using a dedicated enum (instead of binding directly to catalog scopes) keeps toolbar and content switching readable at the tab root.

sections.title: Scoped content and toolbar
sections.explanation: The body swaps `CarCostListContent` and `PersonalExpenseListView` with a smooth transition keyed by scope. The principal toolbar is a segmented picker; leading shows a vehicle menu on car scope or budgets on personal; trailing opens categories and the appropriate add sheet. Add car cost is disabled when no active vehicle is resolved.

sections.title: Active vehicle menu
sections.explanation: `vehicleMenu` lists all queried vehicles and selects via `activeVehicleStore`, marking the current vehicle with a checkmark. This keeps car-cost entry scoped to the same active vehicle used elsewhere in the app without burying vehicle selection inside the list content.

rea-target/FUELIO_FEATURE_MAP.md.overview: Parity checklist mapping Fuelio 10.9.4 capabilities to what FuelTrack already mirrors versus what remains. Tour step 13 uses this document alongside smoke scripts to ground verification and roadmap expectations.

sections.title: Source attribution
sections.explanation: The heading states the comparison target (Fuelio 10.9.4) and that the map was derived from static strings/class names in an unpacked APKM. That provenance clarifies these are feature-level observations, not a runtime API contract.

sections.title: Mirrored capabilities
sections.explanation: The “Mirrored in FuelTrack now” list covers dashboard stats, fuel and cost logs, nearby prices, reminders, multi-vehicle, fuel grades, CSV import/export, GBP/INR settings, and GPS trip log. Reading this against the tour shows which code paths (Fuelio import, FuelStats, trips, spend) already close the gap.

sections.title: Not mirrored yet
sections.explanation: Outstanding Fuelio features include CarPlay/Android Auto, receipt scan, widgets, cloud backup, a historical fill-up map, weather on fill-ups, and premium UI. Native on-device JSON backup is separate from the cloud-backup gap called out here.

Scripts/backup-roundtrip-smoke.swift.overview: Standalone Swift script that encodes and decodes a v2 FuelTrackBackup-shaped fixture, asserts nested IDs and trip points survive, and checks v1 vehicles without `trips` decode to an empty array. Part of tour step 13’s device-free verification suite.

sections.title: Mirrored Codable schema
sections.explanation: The script re-declares Snapshot and nested backup structs so it can run with `swift` without linking the app target. Field layouts intentionally match `FuelTrackBackupExporter` so encode/decode failures here flag schema drift early.

sections.title: V1 trips compatibility types
sections.explanation: `VehicleBackupV1` omits `trips` entirely; `VehicleBackupV2Compat` mirrors the app’s custom decoder that defaults missing trips to `[]`. Together they prove older backups remain readable after the v2 trip fields landed.

sections.title: Fixture encode and assertions
sections.explanation: A fixed-epoch fixture includes vehicle, fill-up, cost, reminder, station, trip with two points, personal expense, overall budget, and a custom category. After ISO-8601 round-trip, the script asserts counts and key IDs, then decodes a v1 vehicle and confirms empty trips, and finally sanity-checks rejecting a non-FuelTrack format name.

Scripts/fuelio-import-smoke.swift.overview: Minimal CSV smoke test that parses a Fuelio multi-section export and asserts vehicle name/fuel unit plus 48 valid fill-up rows. Supports tour step 13 verification of Fuelio CSV shape without the full app importer.

sections.title: CSV and section helpers
sections.explanation: `parseCSVRow` handles quoted fields and escaped quotes; `section` finds `## Name` markers and returns non-empty lines until the next section. These helpers approximate how Fuelio’s multi-section CSV is sliced before row mapping.

sections.title: Fixture assertions
sections.explanation: The script loads a path argument or the default sample CSV, asserts Vehicle Name/FuelUnit, checks Log headers include Date and a Fuel volume column, then counts rows with Date, odometer, and litres present. Expecting exactly 48 fill-ups makes regressions in sample data or parsing obvious.

Scripts/fuelstats-smoke.swift.overview: Standalone smoke test that copies FuelStats full-tank segment math and asserts distance, litres, and L/100km for a three-fill fixture. Tour step 13 uses it to verify economy formulas without a device or SwiftData.

sections.title: Units and segment types
sections.explanation: A minimal `OdometerUnit` converts miles to kilometres; `FillUpSnapshot` and `ConsumptionSegment` mirror the fields the real FuelStats engine needs. `litersPer100km` guards against zero distance or litres before computing the rate.

sections.title: Full-tank segment builder
sections.explanation: `segments(from:)` sorts by odometer then date, ignores skipped fills (resetting the open segment), and only closes a consumption window between successive full tanks. Litres and cost between those anchors become one segment—the same full-tank method described in the README and FuelStats service.

sections.title: Numeric assertions
sections.explanation: The fixture is full → partial → full over 300 miles with 45 litres between full tanks. Assertions check a single segment, distance, litres, and L/100km against the miles-to-km conversion, then print PASS with the computed economy figure.
